newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude eases with WTI, buyers scarce.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude eases with WTI, buyers scarce.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes eased under pressure from West Texas Intermediate (WTI) early Thursday, while continued firmness in futures worried California buyers.

Spot prices for benchmark December WTI crude fell 10 cents from Wednesday to $24.10/24.20 a barrel, under selling pressure. With differentials for Alaska North Slope (ANS) flat at a $2.20 discount, outright ANS prices fell to $21.80/22.10 a barrel.
But crude futures continued this week's rally, rising as much as 33 cents over Wednesday and hitting $24.45 a barrel.
A higher NYMEX helped turned away ANS buyers, who also saw the grade's discount shrink to $2.20 a barrel earlier this week from $2.30 last month.
Traders said a major West Coast refiner bought the ANS on Monday because of a brief respite from the NYMEX crude rally.
"I hate to see the diff go in," one trader said. He added his refinery is considering further run cuts after trimming production 5,000 barrels-a-day late last month.
Weak margins are keeping refiners from buying higher prices crudes, traders and analysts said.

West Coast players said they dismissed Wednesday's API report which showed a five-million-barrel-decrease in the region's supplies. Much of the decrease involves waterborne supplies which are difficult to track, according to traders.
Line 63 crude remained thinly traded in typical early month discussion. The grade, like ANS, fell with WTI prices to $20.90/21.20 a barrel.
Wilmington crude was $17.60/$17.70 a barrel, while Kern River crude stayed $16.15/$16.35 a barrel.
